## Round 41 — Full Change Log

A long follow-up round covering a new site-compatibility report, a repeated slowness complaint, a repeated mobile date-filter complaint, a button-centering complaint, and four new feature/bug requests (bookmark removal, header auto-hide, keep-awake, and another pass over "My History").

### 1. roliascan.com Chapter 1 reported as LOCKED/REMOVED — confirmed correct, no code change
**Report:** MangaFlow said "Chapter 1 may be LOCKED or REMOVED... MangaFlow cannot log in for you" for a chapter on roliascan.com.
**Investigation:** fetched the chapter page directly to check whether this was a false alarm (like round 39's weloma.net/rawkuma.net reports turned out to be). It is not — the page itself shows a **"Login Required"** modal ("Create a free account to continue reading and unlock all chapters") together with an **"Access Restricted — This content is not available anymore"** notice. roliascan.com itself is blocking this specific chapter behind a login wall (or has pulled it), independently of MangaFlow. The diagnostic tool's message was accurate; there is nothing in MangaFlow's own code to fix here. If the manga is otherwise readable on that site when logged in, that is expected — MangaFlow (correctly, for safety) never logs in anywhere on your behalf.

### 2. General site slowness — re-audited, nothing further found
Re-checked the whole app for anything that could be adding to page/chapter load time since round 39's scroll-save fix (which was a confirmed, real slowdown, now fixed). Reviewed the Keeper's background preload interval, the proxy page-cleaning pass, and everything added in rounds 39-40 (wake-lock timer, bookmark checkboxes, date-filter listeners) — none of it runs on a hot path or adds meaningful cost; the new wake-lock safety timer (round 41, #6 below) only fires once every 15 seconds and does nothing when the lock is already held. **This needs more specific information to debug further**: please say exactly where it feels slow next time (the home page loading, opening a chapter, switching chapters, searching another site, something else) and roughly how slow — "slow" by itself does not point at any one piece of code, and changing the page-cleaning security pass by guesswork risks weakening it for no proven benefit.

### 3. My History: Export button not quite centred (profiles.js)
**Root cause:** the dialog is attached to `<body>`, which sets a comfortable **line-height of 1.45** for reading paragraphs. A button's label is one short line, not a paragraph, so that line-height was adding invisible space above and below the text/icon ("half-leading") — the button was already centred by `justify-content`/`align-items`, but centring the *line box* is not quite the same as centring the *ink* when the line box is taller than it needs to be, especially with a symbol character like the "Sync now" ⟲ arrow, whose glyph shape sits differently inside its line than plain letters.
**Fix:** `line-height:1` added to `.mfp-btn`, so the line box now hugs the text/icon exactly and the existing centring lands in the true middle of the button.

### 4. Bookmarks could be added but never removed (profiles.js)
**Problem:** the star button only ever added a bookmark; there was no way to take one back off from inside the Profile window, and no way to remove several at once.
**Fix:** every bookmark row now has its own **×** button (the same single-item-removal pattern "Continue reading" rows already had since round 35) for a quick one-at-a-time removal, PLUS a checkbox on each row and a **"Select all" / "Remove selected (N)"** bar above the list for removing several at once. Removing a bookmark (one or many) immediately tells the home page to redraw its bookmark section and star icons, the same way deleting a history entry already did.

### 5. My History date filter — still broken on some phones, second pass (profiles.js)
Round 40 fixed the *layout* (the date boxes were being squeezed too narrow to use). This round targets the *event handling*, which round 40 did not touch:
- Some phones were found not to reliably fire the `'change'` event at all after picking a date from their native calendar widget — only `'input'`. The filter now also listens on `'input'`, but **only acts when the value is already a complete, valid date** (an incomplete value is simply ignored, never resets the filter) — so this cannot reintroduce round 39's original bug.
- The dialog's own re-render (which rebuilds the date `<input>` element from scratch) now happens a moment later (`setTimeout(…, 0)`) instead of instantly inside the event handler, giving a phone's native picker-closing animation/focus-return sequence time to fully finish first, instead of potentially having its own `<input>` element torn out from under it mid-sequence.

### 6. "Keep screen awake" stopped working partway through a session (app.js)
**Root cause (two found):**
- The switch correctly asked for a Screen Wake Lock, but some phones' own aggressive battery-saving software (several Android makers are known for this) can silently take the lock away without the browser ever firing an event MangaFlow was listening for, and nothing then asked for it again until the phone happened to trigger one of those events — which, left untouched on a desk, might be never.
- Separately found: saving settings was writing `keepAwake:true` straight into permanent storage, even though round 38 explicitly said this switch must *never* persist across a reload (for battery/privacy reasons) — a real inconsistency, now fixed, though not the direct cause of the screen going dark mid-session.
**Fix:** a 15-second safety-net timer re-asks for the lock whenever it isn't currently held (harmless no-op if it already is), plus re-asking on the next tap or touch (a few browsers only allow a fresh request from inside a user action). The switch's own live state is untouched by storage now, so it keeps working normally for the rest of the visit either way. **If a specific phone still dims/locks the screen after this**, that phone's own battery/app-optimisation setting for the browser being used likely needs to be turned off by hand in the phone's own Settings app — that part is outside what any website's code can override.

### 7. Header auto-hiding too eagerly while reading (app.js)
**Problem:** scrolling up to reach the header/buttons while reading could show them for barely a second before they hid again.
**Root cause:** showing AND hiding the header both required a recent (within 1.5s) tap-to-scroll action — drag-scrolling or simply pausing for a moment closed that window, after which scrolling up could no longer bring the header back at all until a tap happened to line up with it again, which felt random.
**Fix:** showing the header on scroll-up no longer needs that "recent tap" gate at all (showing is always safe); hiding still requires it, so an automatic/background scroll can never sneak in a hide. A short 900ms hold after showing also blocks any hide right afterward, so a little scroll jitter the moment the header reappears cannot immediately hide it again. A touch starting now also counts as "recent input" (not just an explicit tap-to-scroll), so hiding still works properly for people who read by dragging rather than tapping.
**Not possible without a bigger change:** the request to also auto-hide the top bar while *browsing other manga sites* (not reading) cannot be done the same way — the mini-browser's `Content-Security-Policy: script-src 'none'` (blocking all third-party JavaScript, a core safety rule of the whole proxy design since round 8) means a site being browsed cannot report anything about its own scroll position back to MangaFlow at all, by design. Doing this would require either running the other site's JavaScript (removing that safety rule) or rebuilding the mini-browser as a true scroll-synced native frame, which is a much larger change — happy to scope that separately if it's wanted badly enough to accept the trade-off.

### 8. A full pass over "every button, shortcut and option" (scope note)
Went through the items explicitly named this round (all above) plus a re-check of the buttons/shortcuts touched directly by those fixes (header buttons, Settings' keep-awake switch, the Profile window's every tab). A genuine, exhaustive click-through of *every* option on a real phone is not something that can be done from here without an actual device in hand — please flag anything specific that still looks or acts wrong after this round, the same way the screenshot and roliascan.com report were used this time, so it can be checked with real evidence instead of guesswork.

## Round 42 — Full Change Log

The owner reported that round 41's fixes (Export button, date filter, header-hide) looked completely unchanged on their phone, despite the GitHub push having genuinely succeeded. That mismatch pointed at something bigger than any one button.

### 1. Found the real reason earlier rounds could look like they "never arrived": no cache-busting (index.html)
**Root cause:** every single round, every file kept the exact same name and address — `app.js`, `profiles.js`, `style.css`, and so on, every time. A browser's cache (and, on mobile data, sometimes the phone carrier's own network-level cache too) decides whether it already has a file **purely by that address** — it has no way to know the *contents* at that address changed on the server unless the address itself changes or it happens to re-check. With the same address reused round after round, a phone could easily keep running JavaScript from several rounds ago while genuinely believing it was looking at "the site" — making brand-new, correctly-deployed fixes look like they had never been applied at all, which matches exactly what was reported.
**Fix:** every local `<script src="...">` and `<link rel="stylesheet" href="...">` tag in `index.html` now ends in `?v=42` (see the long comment right above them). Changing that number forces every browser to treat the file as a completely new address it has never cached before — a clean, forced re-download, every round, no exceptions. **Going forward this number will be bumped automatically whenever these files change**, so this class of problem should not come back. **One-time action needed on your end:** since this fix only takes effect once the new `index.html` itself is loaded fresh, please do ONE hard refresh / "clear site data" for the MangaFlow address on your phone after this update goes live — after that one time, this mechanism keeps everything current automatically.

### 2. Header now also hides while scrolling MangaFlow's own search/start page (app.js, style.css)
Re-read the round 41 note that said hiding the header while browsing *another* site's content is technically impossible (that still stands — see below). But browsing **MangaFlow's own search results and start page** is a different story: that content lives in `#viewport`, which is MangaFlow's own element and fires normal scroll events MangaFlow can read. **Added:** the header now hides on scroll-down and reappears on scroll-up while looking at MangaFlow's own start page / search results, the same behaviour reading mode's header already had. It is reset to visible automatically the moment you navigate anywhere else, so it can never get stuck hidden on a different screen.
**Still not possible:** hiding the header while an *external* site is open inside the mini-browser iframe. That site's scrolling happens inside its own separate document, which MangaFlow cannot read (a different website) and whose JavaScript is completely blocked by design (`script-src 'none'`, a core security rule since round 8) — so there is no signal, from either side, that could ever reach MangaFlow. This is a hard technical wall of the current proxy design, not an oversight.

### 3. Re-confirmed: Export button + date filter code from round 41 is correct and already deployed
Re-checked both pieces of code line by line again: the Export button's `line-height:1` fix and the date filter's dual `input`/`change` handling are both syntactically valid and present in the pushed commit. Given finding #1 above, the most likely explanation for these "still" not working is that the phone was running cached code from before round 40/41 ever reached it. Please re-test after the one-time cache clear mentioned in #1 — if either one is still visibly wrong after that, a fresh screenshot showing the current (round 42) state would help pin down anything genuinely still open, the same way it did for the original Export-button report.

## How to Improve Further

### Translation quality
- Run a real translation API (DeepL, Google Translate) instead of on-device — better for long sentences
- Cache translations so re-opening a chapter is instant
- Let the user edit individual bubble translations

### PDF export
- Pre-translate all pages before the download starts (currently only translated pages get overlays)
- Support multi-column text reflowing
- Let the user choose font size

### Chapter loading
- Cache the chapter list in localStorage so it loads instantly on revisit
- Show a progress bar during `morePages()` pagination

### History / Cloud
- Add per-chapter progress (page number saved, not just "read")
- Add a "currently reading" shelf separate from history
- Show reading streaks / stats

### Accounts Worker
- PBKDF2 instead of SHA-256 for code hashing (needs paid Workers plan for more CPU)
- E-mail recovery option
- Cron Trigger to auto-delete old history rows daily
- Per-day reading chart for the admin

---

## Security Notes

- **keepAwake**: Always resets to `false` on page load. Never persists across reloads.
- **Tokens**: 30-day expiry. Stored in D1. Cleaned up on each login.
- **Code hashing**: SHA-256(PEPPER + salt + user + code). Never the raw code.
- **Fail lock**: 5 wrong tries → 15-minute lockout per username.
- **CORS**: Set `ALLOWED_ORIGINS` in the Worker to your GitHub Pages URL.
- **CSP (index.html)**: `script-src 'self' 'wasm-unsafe-eval'` — no inline scripts, no CDN.

### File: `index.html`  (667 lines)

**Why this file exists / what it does:** The page itself (Page 1 start page, Page 2 site view frame, Page 3 reading mode, all dialogs and settings). Loads every other file in a fixed order.

~~~~~~html
-->

<html lang="en" data-theme="light">

  <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1, viewport-fit=cover, interactive-widget=resizes-content">

  <!-- WHY: colours the phone's browser bar to match the site. app.js updates it when the theme changes. -->
  <meta name="theme-color" content="#ffffff">

  <meta name="referrer" content="no-referrer">

       LIMIT: a <meta> policy cannot set frame-ancestors. Use the _headers file (see MANGAFLOW.md) on hosts that allow headers.
       IMPROVE: tighten connect-src to your own proxy addresses once you only use those. -->
  <meta http-equiv="Content-Security-Policy" content="default-src 'self'; script-src 'self' 'wasm-unsafe-eval' https://cse.google.com https://www.google.com https://www.gstatic.com https://clients1.google.com https://clients1.google.co.in https://*.google.com https://partner.googleadservices.com https://*.googleadservices.com https://pagead2.googlesyndication.com https://*.googlesyndication.com https://syndicatedsearch.goog https://*.syndicatedsearch.goog; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline' https:; img-src * data: blob:; media-src * blob:; font-src * data:; connect-src *; frame-src 'self' about: blob: data: https://*.google.com https://*.google.co.in https://*.googleapis.com https://*.gstatic.com https://*.googlesyndication.com https://*.googleadservices.com https://*.doubleclick.net https://*.syndicatedsearch.goog https://syndicatedsearch.goog https://www.google.com https://googleads.g.doubleclick.net https://syndicatedsearch.goog https://*.syndicatedsearch.goog https://*.google.com https://*.googlesyndication.com; object-src 'none'; form-action 'self'">

  <title>MangaFlow Reader</title>
  <!-- ROUND 42 FIX (version number now 43) — this is very likely the REAL reason several earlier rounds' fixes looked like they "never
       arrived" even after confirming the push to GitHub went through fine: GitHub Pages, and especially mobile
       carriers/browsers, can keep serving an OLD cached copy of style.css / app.js / profiles.js / etc. for a
       while after a new version is deployed, because every round reused the exact same file name and address,
       which is the one thing a cache uses to decide "have I already got this?". WHY the fix: every local
       stylesheet/script tag below now ends in "?v=69" — changing that number is a tiny edit to THIS file, but it
       makes the browser treat it as a brand-new address it has never cached before, forcing a fresh download
       every time, with no stale leftovers possible, regardless of how long a phone or carrier would otherwise
       hold onto the old copy. HOW TO KEEP THIS WORKING: bump every "?v=69" below to the new round's number
       whenever ANY of these specific files changes in a future round (a quick find-and-replace) — Claude will
       keep doing this automatically going forward. IMPROVE: a build step that computes this automatically from
       each file's own content hash, so it can never be forgotten by hand. -->
  <link rel="stylesheet" href="style.css?v=69">
  <!-- ROUND 29: boot.js runs BEFORE the first paint. WHY: so a refresh / reopen shows the cover "Reopening where you were..." (below) and the saved dark theme at once,
       instead of flashing the start page while the big app.js loads. HOW: it only reads the address and the saved settings. IMPROVE: none needed. It is safe to remove (the flash returns). -->
  <script src="boot.js?v=69"></script>
</head>
<body data-side="right">

  <!-- ROUND 29: THE REOPEN COVER. WHY: while the page address asks for a reopen (#r= #p= #q=), this covers the start screen from the first paint; style.css shows it only
       while <html> has the class mf-resuming (boot.js adds it, app.js removes it). HOW: a fixed full-screen box with a spinner and one line; role=status so a screen reader says it.
       IMPROVE: show the title of the page that is being reopened. -->
  <div id="resume" role="status" aria-live="polite"><div class="spinner" aria-hidden="true"></div><p>Reopening where you were&hellip;</p><div id="resumeSlow" hidden><p>This is taking longer than usual. The site may be slow or blocking MangaFlow.</p><button type="button" id="resumeHome" class="primary">Open the start page</button></div></div>

  <!-- =====================================================================
       BROWSER VIEW  (the "mini browser": address bar + page area)
       WHY: The user types a manga site/URL here; app.js fetches it and shows it in the frame.
       IMPROVE: Add tabs, or a "recently read" row with cover thumbnails.
       ===================================================================== -->
  <div id="browser">
    <header class="navbar">
      <button id="btnBack" title="Back" aria-label="Back">&#8592;</button>
      <button id="btnFwd" title="Forward" aria-label="Forward">&#8594;</button>
      <button id="btnReload" title="Reload" aria-label="Reload">&#10227;</button>
      <button id="btnHome" title="Start page" aria-label="Start page">&#8962;</button>

      <!-- WIDE SCREENS: a normal address form.
           WHY: a <form> gives us "press Enter to go" for free on both keyboards and phones.
           inputmode="url" shows the URL keyboard on phones. font-size 16px in CSS stops iOS auto-zoom. -->
      <form id="addrForm" autocomplete="off">
        <span class="inwrap"><input id="addr" type="text" inputmode="url" autocapitalize="off" autocorrect="off" spellcheck="false"
               placeholder="Paste a manga URL or type a name to search" aria-label="Address or search"><button type="button" class="clearx" data-for="addr" hidden title="Clear" aria-label="Clear the box">&#10005;</button></span>
        <button type="submit" class="primary">Go</button>
      </form>

      <!-- NARROW SCREENS (phones, small windows): the form above is hidden by CSS and this "pill" is shown.
           Tapping it opens the floating search bar (#searchPop below). -->
      <button id="addrPill" type="button" aria-label="Search or paste a link">
        <span aria-hidden="true">&#128269;</span><span id="pillText">Search or paste a link</span>
      </button>

      <button id="btnStar" title="Bookmark this page" aria-label="Bookmark">&#9734;</button>
      <button id="btnThemeB" title="Toggle white / black" aria-label="Toggle theme">&#9680;</button>
      <!-- ROUND 18: full-screen button for the regular page (hidden when Settings > Search & extras > "Full-screen button" is off) -->
      <button id="btnFsNav" class="fs-btn" title="Full screen (Esc leaves it)" aria-label="Full screen">&#9974;</button>
      <button id="btnSettings" title="Settings" aria-label="Settings">&#9881;</button>
    </header>

    <!-- ROUND 39: "Open on <site>" — shown ONLY while an actual page of an external manga site is open in the
         mini-browser (never on the start page or a search results list — see updateNav() in app.js). Tapping it
         opens that exact page on the real site in a new tab, for when a button/script on the original page does
         not work through MangaFlow's proxy. Hidden by default; app.js un-hides it.
         ROUND 40: redesigned from a wide text pill (which floated over the middle of the page and looked out of
         place next to the real site's own content, and on phones got moved down near the bottom where it
         overlapped the "Reading mode" button) into a small ICON-ONLY button, the same size/shape as the other
         toolbar buttons above (Back, Forward, Reload, Star, Theme, Settings, etc.) and always pinned just under
         the header's right side, on every screen size — never at the bottom. &#8599; is the universal "opens
         outside this page" arrow. Styled and positioned in style.css (search "btnOrigSite"). -->
    <button id="btnOrigSite" type="button" title="Open this page on the original site" aria-label="Open on the original site" hidden>&#8599;</button>

    <!-- WHY: thin progress line shown while a page is loading (feedback on slow proxies). -->
    <div id="loadbar"></div>

    <!-- ROUND 15: slim notice shown when a normal website may look incomplete (styles / icon fonts not loaded, or a page that is built by JavaScript).
         WHY: people asked for a bug report whenever something is wrong. HOW: app.js (pageHealth) fills the text and a copyable report; Report opens
         the big error pop-up, Open original opens the real site in a new tab, X hides it. IMPROVE: remember "do not warn again for this site". -->
    <div id="pageNote" hidden role="status"><span id="pageNoteText"></span>
      <button type="button" id="pageNoteReport">Report</button><button type="button" id="pageNoteOpen">Open original</button><button type="button" id="pageNoteX" aria-label="Dismiss">&#10005;</button></div>

    <main id="viewport">
      <!-- Start page: shown until the first page is opened. -->
      <section id="start">
        <!-- ROUND 10: a friendlier start page. HERO = the big search card; STEPS = how it works; then your lists as cards.
             WHY: the old page was one grey paragraph. HOW: plain HTML + CSS (gradient, cards); app.js fills the lists and chips.
             IMPROVE: add cover thumbnails, a "trending" row, and a dark/light preview. -->
        <div class="hero">
          <div class="hero-badge">&#128214; MangaFlow</div>
          <h2>Read any manga in one endless scroll</h2>
          <p class="hero-sub">Paste a series or chapter link. It opens straight in reading mode.</p>
          <form id="heroForm" autocomplete="off">
            <span class="inwrap"><input id="addrHero" type="text" inputmode="url" autocapitalize="off" autocorrect="off" spellcheck="false"
                   placeholder="Paste a manga link, or type a name to search" aria-label="Manga link or search words"><button type="button" class="clearx" data-for="addrHero" hidden title="Clear" aria-label="Clear the box">&#10005;</button></span>
            <button type="button" id="heroPaste" title="Paste from clipboard" aria-label="Paste">&#128203;</button>
            <button type="button" id="heroClip" class="clipdd" title="Clipboard list" aria-label="Clipboard list">&#9662;</button>
            <button type="submit" class="primary">Read</button>
          </form>
          <!-- ROUND 15: Manga / Everything switch. WHY: typing words searches the web; "Manga" adds the word manga to the search, "Everything" does not.
               Typing a site name such as any.com always opens that site. -->
          <div id="scopeSwitch" class="scope" role="group" aria-label="Search scope"><span>SEARCH</span><button type="button" data-scope="manga" class="on" aria-pressed="true">Manga</button><button type="button" data-scope="all" aria-pressed="false">Everything</button></div>
          <!-- ROUND 16: search engine choice. WHY: if one free engine asks for a CAPTCHA, the next one is tried automatically (we never solve CAPTCHAs).
               "Auto" = Bing, Mojeek, Yahoo, DuckDuckGo, Brave in that order (ENGINE_ORDER in app.js). ROUND 28b: the Google button searches the typed words INSIDE MangaFlow (your Programmable Search
               panel, or the Google API when a key is set); only an EMPTY box opens google.com in a new tab. -->
          <div id="engineRow" class="scope engine" role="group" aria-label="Search engine"><span>ENGINE</span>
            <select id="engineSel" aria-label="Search engine"><option value="google">Google (your search)</option><option value="auto">Auto (free engines)</option><option value="bing">Bing</option><option value="mojeek">Mojeek</option><option value="yahoo">Yahoo</option><option value="duckduckgo">DuckDuckGo</option><option value="brave">Brave</option></select>
            <button type="button" id="googleBtn" title="Search these words with Google inside MangaFlow">Google</button></div>
          <div id="statusChips" class="status-chips" aria-label="Status"></div>
          <!-- ROUND 15: live status strip (drawn by app.js drawHud every second while this page is visible) -->
          <div id="hud" class="hud" aria-label="System status"></div>
        </div>

        <div class="steps">
          <div class="step"><b>1</b><span>Paste a link</span><small>series page or any chapter</small></div>
          <div class="step"><b>2</b><span>Scroll to read</span><small>chapters load by themselves, up and down</small></div>
          <div class="step"><b>3</b><span>Download a PDF</span><small>see the file size first</small></div>
        </div>

        <!-- WHY: shows the manga, the site and the exact chapter you stopped at. Tap one to continue there. -->
        <h3>Continue reading</h3>
        <div id="readList" class="list cards"></div>
        <h3>Recent pages</h3>
        <div id="recentList" class="list"></div>
        <h3>Bookmarks</h3>
        <div id="bookList" class="list"></div>
        <p class="muted small">Only read content you have the right to access.</p>
      </section>

      <!-- WHY sandbox: we render the other site's HTML inside an iframe. "allow-same-origin" lets OUR script
           attach click handlers to its links. We deliberately do NOT allow scripts, so nothing from the
           other site can run. "allow-forms" lets site-search forms fire events we can intercept.
           IMPROVE: add a "desktop site" toggle by sending a different User-Agent through your own proxy. -->
      <iframe id="frame" title="Page" sandbox="allow-same-origin allow-forms allow-popups allow-popups-to-escape-sandbox" referrerpolicy="no-referrer" hidden></iframe>

      <!-- ROUND 18: GOOGLE SEARCH PANEL.
           WHY: the owner made a Google Programmable Search Engine (cx c0d44f55eddb847e4). Google draws its search box and its result list
                INSIDE this panel, so searching works like a normal search without any proxy.
           HOW: app.js (section 18) loads https://cse.google.com/cse.js?cx=... only when it is needed, draws the element in #gvBox and calls
                execute(words). A tap on a result is caught and opened INSIDE MangaFlow (reading mode when it is a manga page).
           IMPROVE: add a "search again on Bing" button when Google shows no results. -->
      <section id="gview" hidden aria-label="Google search">
        <div class="gv-bar"><b>&#128269; Google</b><span id="gvQuery" class="muted small"></span>
          <button type="button" id="gvTab" title="Open this search on google.com in a new tab">google.com &#8599;</button>
          <button type="button" id="gvClose" title="Close the Google panel">&#10005; Close</button></div>
        <div id="gvStatus" class="muted small" role="status"></div>
        <div id="gvBox"></div>
      </section>
    </main>

    <!-- Floating corner button: appears once a page is loaded. -->
    <!-- ROUND 56: icon only (no words), so it covers as little of the original site as possible. The name is kept for screen readers in aria-label and for a mouse in title. -->
    <button id="fabRead" hidden aria-label="Reading mode" title="Reading mode">&#128214;</button>
    <!-- ROUND 56: tiny chapter bar for Page 2 (previous / chapter list / next). Shown by app.js only on a chapter page whose own chapter buttons cannot be found. -->
    <div id="p2NavBar" hidden><button id="p2Prev" aria-label="Previous chapter" title="Previous chapter">&#8249;</button><button id="p2List" aria-label="Chapter list" title="Chapter list">&#9776;</button><button id="p2Next" aria-label="Next chapter" title="Next chapter">&#8250;</button></div>
  </div>

  <!-- =====================================================================
       READER VIEW  (reading mode)
       WHY: Hidden until the user presses the reading-mode button. Uses normal window scrolling so
            mobile browsers can hide their own toolbars while you scroll (more room for the art).
       IMPROVE: Add a "page-by-page" mode (swipe left/right) for people who dislike vertical scroll.
       ===================================================================== -->
  <div id="reader" hidden>
    <!-- ROUND 9: the reading-progress line is NOT inside the title bar any more. WHY: the whole bar now SLIDES UP out of
         the screen while you scroll down (CSS transform). A line inside it would be trapped by that transform, and before
         it was left floating in the middle of the page. Here it is pinned to the very top edge of the screen instead, so
         it stays a thin 3 px line that never covers the pictures. app.js changes its width ($('#progress i')). -->
    <div id="progress" aria-hidden="true"><i></i></div>

    <!-- class "ui-hide": the buttons fade out while you scroll DOWN and come back when you scroll UP; the whole bar also
         slides up (ROUND 9) so nothing is left behind on the page. -->
    <header id="readerBar">
      <div class="rb-row">
        <button id="btnHomeR" class="ui-hide" title="Go to the start page" aria-label="Start page">&#8962;</button>
        <button id="btnExit" class="ui-hide" title="Exit reading mode (Esc)">&#10005;<span class="lbl"> End reading</span></button>
        <!-- ROUND 8: the title now has class ui-hide too, so it fades away while you scroll down (like the buttons)
             and comes back when you scroll up. -->
        <div class="rb-title ui-hide">
          <h1 id="rTitle">Manga</h1>
          <span id="rSub"></span>
        </div>
        <button id="btnChapters" class="ui-hide" title="Chapter list (C)">&#9776; &#9662;</button>
        <button id="btnTheme" class="ui-hide" title="Toggle white / black (T)">&#9680;</button>
        <button id="btnSettingsR" class="ui-hide" title="Settings, clear chapter cache" aria-label="Settings">&#9881;</button>
      </div>
      <!-- ROUND 8: search / link bar INSIDE reading mode. Paste another manga link and press Read: the site is opened
           and read straight away. Typing words (not a link) leaves reading mode and shows the search results.
           It hides on scroll down and returns on scroll up, like everything else in this bar. -->
      <form id="rdForm" class="rb-search ui-hide" autocomplete="off">
        <span class="inwrap"><input id="rdAddr" type="text" inputmode="url" autocapitalize="off" autocorrect="off" spellcheck="false"
               placeholder="Paste a manga link to read it, or type a name to search" aria-label="Link or search words"><button type="button" class="clearx" data-for="rdAddr" hidden title="Clear" aria-label="Clear the box">&#10005;</button></span>
        <button type="submit" class="primary" title="Open and read this link">Read</button>
      </form>
    </header>

    <!-- Chapter dropdown: clicking an entry jumps to that chapter. The first button makes the PDF. -->
    <div id="chapterMenu" hidden>
      <button id="btnDlMenu" class="primary dl-menu">&#11015; Download chapters (PDF)&hellip;</button>
      <!-- ROUND 18: full screen, right below the download button -->
      <button id="btnFsMenu" class="dl-menu fs-btn">&#9974; Full screen</button>
      <button id="btnFreeMenu" class="dl-menu">&#129529; Free memory (clear chapter cache)&hellip;</button>
      <ul id="chapterList"></ul>
    </div>

    <!-- ROUND 9: EARLIER CHAPTERS BAR.
         WHY: when you open a link of chapter 5 directly, reading starts at chapter 5. This bar sits above it and lets
              you load chapters 4, 3, 2, 1 (above, without losing your place). They also load by themselves when you
              scroll UP near the top, or press the "up" round key / Left arrow at the first chapter.
         HOW: app.js loadPrev() fills it (text in #prevInfo, button #btnPrevLoad). It always keeps the same height, so the
              page never jumps when it has nothing more to offer.
         IMPROVE: show the names of the earlier chapters here. -->
    <div id="prevBar">
      <button id="btnPrevLoad" type="button">&#9650; Load earlier chapters</button>
      <span id="prevInfo" class="muted small"></span>
    </div>

    <!-- All chapters get appended here, one after another. -->
    <main id="stream"></main>

    <!-- WHY: invisible marker. When it comes near the screen, app.js loads the next chapter. -->
    <div id="sentinel"></div>

    <!-- DOWNLOAD BAR: at the end of the page. Appears as soon as one chapter is loaded. -->
    <section id="dlBar" hidden>
      <p id="dlInfo" class="muted"></p>
      <button id="btnDl" class="primary">&#11015; Download chapters (PDF)&hellip;</button>
      <!-- ROUND 18: full screen, right below the download button -->
      <button id="btnFsDl" class="fs-btn">&#9974; Full screen</button>
      <p class="muted small">Choose which chapters (for example 1&ndash;50). One PDF named after the manga, every chapter is ONE long page like the reading mode, full quality. You can keep reading while it downloads.</p>
    </section>

    <div id="theEnd" hidden>
      <p>&#8212; End of the available chapters &#8212;</p>
      <button id="btnTopEnd" class="primary">Back to top</button>
    </div>

    <!-- READER KEYS (round 9: ONE horizontal row of round 3D buttons in the bottom-RIGHT corner; switchable in Settings).
         Order, left to right:
           1. reload THIS chapter        2. reload ALL open chapters
           3. up arrow = previous chapter  4. down arrow = next chapter   (ROUND 11: hidden by CSS while chapter-slider.js is linked: the slider replaces them)
           5. End = jump to the end of everything that is loaded (the real End key on the keyboard does the same).
         Real keyboard: Left / Right arrow = previous / next chapter, End = end of the page.
         The whole row hides while you scroll down and returns when you scroll up.
         The side (right is the default, or left) can be changed in Settings. -->
    <!-- ROUND 9b: the two RELOAD keys stay in the bottom-LEFT corner; the previous / next / end keys form one horizontal
         row in the bottom-RIGHT corner. #side is a full-width, click-through strip that holds the two groups
         (.kg). The "side" setting now says where the arrow keys live (right = default, left swaps the two groups). -->
    <nav id="side" class="ui-hide" aria-label="Reader keys">
      <div class="kg kg-l">
        <!-- ROUND 12: the two reload keys were REMOVED. Their job is done by the reload wheel (reload-wheel.js) in this corner:
             turn it right = reload this chapter, turn it left = reload all chapters. -->
        <!-- ROUND 10: scroll to the top of the page (same round 3D look as the reload keys; the Home key does the same) -->
        <button id="btnTop" class="key k-top" title="Go to the top of the page (Home key)" aria-label="Go to the top">&#8679;</button>
      </div>
      <div class="kg kg-r">
        <button id="btnPrev" class="key k-up" title="Previous chapter (Left arrow)" aria-label="Previous chapter">&#8593;</button>
        <button id="btnNext" class="key k-down" title="Next chapter (Right arrow)" aria-label="Next chapter">&#8595;</button>
        <button id="btnEnd" class="key k-end" title="Go to the end of the loaded chapters (End key)" aria-label="Go to the end">&#8615;</button>
      </div>
    </nav>
  </div>

  <!-- Small shared widgets -->
  <div id="busy" hidden></div>
  <!-- ROUND 18: the button that leaves full screen (shown only in full screen; Esc does the same). It is pinned in the top-right corner. -->
  <button id="fsExit" type="button" hidden title="Leave full screen (Esc)" aria-label="Leave full screen">&#10005; Exit full screen</button>

  <!-- DOWNLOAD DOCK (round 7): floating box in the bottom corner. It stays on screen in every view until the
       downloads are finished or closed, shows the PDF size while it grows, and can be minimised to a small pill. -->
  <!-- ROUND 8: the dock now sits right ABOVE the reader keys (same corner). The round pill shows the progress; tap it to open
       the list. Minimising (or just ignoring) the list NEVER stops a download: only the Cancel button does. -->
  <!-- ROUND 19: full-screen ICON button for reading mode (same symbol as the navbar one, no text). It stands under the download pill and slides with it. -->
  <button id="fsRead" class="fs-btn" type="button" title="Full screen (Esc leaves it)" aria-label="Full screen">&#9974;</button>
  <aside id="dock" class="ui-hide min" hidden aria-label="Downloads">
    <button id="dockIcon" type="button" aria-label="Show or hide downloads">
      <span class="ring"><span class="arrow">&#11015;</span></span>
      <span id="dockLabel">Downloads</span><b id="dockCount"></b>
    </button>
    <div id="dockBox">
      <div class="dock-head"><b>Downloads</b><span class="muted small">keeps going when minimised</span><button id="dockMin" type="button" title="Minimise (the download keeps running)" aria-label="Minimise downloads">&#8212;</button></div>
      <ul id="dockList"></ul>
    </div>
  </aside>

  <!-- RANGE DIALOG (round 7): which chapters go into the PDF. -->
  <dialog id="rangeDlg">
    <form method="dialog">
      <h3>Download chapters as PDF</h3>
      <p class="muted small">Pick the chapters. Chapters that are not open in reading mode are fetched for you.</p>
      <div id="rgChips" class="chips" role="group" aria-label="Quick ranges"></div>
      <div class="rg-row">
        <label>From <select id="rgFrom"></select></label>
        <label>To <select id="rgTo"></select></label>
      </div>
      <label>Make
        <select id="rgSplit">
          <option value="0">one file</option>
          <option value="25">a new file every 25 chapters</option>
          <option value="50">a new file every 50 chapters</option>
          <option value="100">a new file every 100 chapters</option>
        </select>
      </label>
      <!-- ROUND 10: quality choice and the ESTIMATED FILE SIZE are shown BEFORE you press "Make PDF" -->
      <!-- ROUND 11: four picture qualities. app.js adds "about NN MB" to each line after it measured sample pages. -->
      <label>Picture quality (file size)
        <select id="rgMode">
          <option value="original">Original: pictures exactly as the site sent them (biggest)</option>
          <option value="balanced">Balanced: looks the same, about half the size (recommended)</option>
          <option value="small">Small: slightly softer, pictures at most 1100 px wide</option>
          <option value="tiny">Tiny: for phones with little space, at most 800 px wide</option>
        </select>
      </label>
      <p id="rgSize" class="rg-size" aria-live="polite"></p>
      <p id="rgInfo" class="muted small"></p>
      <div class="row">
        <button type="button" id="rgCancel">Cancel</button>
        <button type="button" id="rgGo" class="primary">Make PDF</button>
      </div>
    </form>
  </dialog>

  <!-- FLOATING SEARCH BAR (phones / narrow windows). Opened by the pill in the address bar. -->
  <!-- ROUND 17: the clipboard list (one shared drop-down, filled and placed by app.js openClip) -->
  <div id="clipPop" hidden role="menu" aria-label="Clipboard list"></div>
  <div id="popShade" hidden></div>
  <div id="searchPop" hidden role="dialog" aria-label="Search or paste a link">
    <form id="popForm" autocomplete="off">
      <span class="inwrap"><input id="addr2" type="text" inputmode="url" autocapitalize="off" autocorrect="off" spellcheck="false"
             placeholder="Paste a link or type a name to search" aria-label="Link or search words"><button type="button" class="clearx" data-for="addr2" hidden title="Clear" aria-label="Clear the box">&#10005;</button></span>
      <button type="button" id="btnPaste" title="Paste from clipboard" aria-label="Paste">&#128203;</button>
      <button type="button" id="popClip" class="clipdd" title="Clipboard list" aria-label="Clipboard list">&#9662;</button>
      <button type="submit" class="primary">Go</button>
    </form>
  </div>

  <!-- ROUND 8: BIG ERROR POP-UP. A modal dialog (centre of the screen, impossible to miss) with a plain summary, a hint
       and a full report you can copy and paste to Claude. app.js showError() fills it in. Global handlers also use it, so
       even unexpected crashes show up here instead of failing silently. -->
  <dialog id="errbox" aria-labelledby="errTitle">
    <h2 id="errTitle">&#9888; Something went wrong</h2>
    <p id="errSummary"></p>
    <p id="errHint" class="muted"></p>
    <textarea id="errText" readonly rows="14" aria-label="Error report"></textarea>
    <div class="row">
      <button id="errClose" type="button">Close</button>
      <button id="errFix" type="button" title="Open Settings > Troubleshoot">&#128295; Troubleshoot</button>
      <button id="errCopy" type="button" class="primary">Copy report</button>
    </div>
  </dialog>
~~~~~~

### File: `style.css`  (1436 lines)

**Why this file exists / what it does:** The whole look of the site: colours (light/dark), header, buttons, reading mode columns, floating keys, dialogs, phone layout. Every block starts with a comment saying why it exists.

<!-- BEGIN FILE: style.css -->
~~~~~~css
/* =====================================================================
   MangaFlow Reader - style.css
   WHY: All visuals live here so changing the look never touches the logic.
   Every block below has:  WHY (reason it exists)  |  IMPROVE (ideas for later)
   ===================================================================== */

/* ---------- 1. THEME VARIABLES ----------
   WHY: Colours are stored once as variables. The theme toggle only flips data-theme on <html>
        and every colour below updates automatically. Light = pure white, dark = pure black (#000).
   HOW: var(--name) in any rule below reads the value. The [data-theme="dark"] block overrides them.
   IMPROVE: Add a third "sepia" theme by adding [data-theme="sepia"] { ... }. */
/* WHY: :root is the top of the page, so these variables are available everywhere. HOW: - -bg is background, - -fg text, */
/* - -muted grey text, - -bar see-through bar colour, - -line thin borders, - -accent orange highlight, - -shadow soft */
/* glow under cards. IMPROVE: move - -accent to Settings so users pick a colour. */
:root {
  --bg: #ffffff;
  --fg: #111111;
  --muted: #666666;
  --bar: rgba(255, 255, 255, .92);
  --line: rgba(0, 0, 0, .14);
  --accent: #e8590c;
  --shadow: 0 14px 44px rgba(0, 0, 0, .20);
  --keytop: #f6f6f6;                            /* keycap colours (arrow keys in reading mode) */
  --keyedge: #b9b9b9;
  --keyhi: #ffffff;                             /* highlight spot on the round 3D keys */
  --w: 820px;                                   /* chapter column width (changed in Settings) */
  --safe-t: env(safe-area-inset-top, 0px);      /* phone notch spacing */
  --safe-b: env(safe-area-inset-bottom, 0px);
}
/* WHY: the dark theme. HOW: when <html> has data-theme='dark', these values replace the ones in :root, so the whole site */
/* turns black without changing any other rule. Missing variables (like - -accent) are simply kept. IMPROVE: also follow */
/* the phone setting with prefers-color-scheme. */
[data-theme="dark"] {
  --bg: #000000;
  --fg: #eeeeee;
  --muted: #9a9a9a;
  --bar: rgba(0, 0, 0, .92);
  --line: rgba(255, 255, 255, .18);
  --shadow: 0 14px 44px rgba(255, 255, 255, .08);
  --keytop: #2d2d2d;
  --keyedge: #1b1b1b;
  --keyhi: #5a5a5a;
}

/* ---------- 2. BASE RESET ----------
   WHY: border-box makes widths predictable; removing the default margin avoids a stray white edge.
        Reduced-motion: people who turn off animations in their system settings get no animations.
   IMPROVE: add more @media (prefers-reduced-motion) rules if you add more animation. */
/* WHY: a reset gives every browser the same starting point. HOW: * means every element. border-box makes padding count */
/* inside the width, so boxes do not overflow. The tap-highlight rule removes the grey flash on phone taps. IMPROVE: add */
/* focus styles if you remove the flash. */
* { box-sizing: border-box; -webkit-tap-highlight-color: transparent; }
/* WHY: browsers add a default margin around the page, which shows as a white edge. HOW: set margin to 0 on html and */
/* body. IMPROVE: none needed. */
html, body { margin: 0; }
/* WHY: sets the default look of the whole site. HOW: background and text colour come from the theme variables; the font */
/* list uses the phone or computer's own font (system-ui) for fast loading; line-height 1.45 gives readable spacing. */
/* IMPROVE: let users pick the font size. */
body {
  background: var(--bg);
  color: var(--fg);
  font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, "Segoe UI", Roboto, sans-serif;
  line-height: 1.45;
}
[hidden] { display: none !important; }          /* WHY: makes the "hidden" attribute always win */
/* WHY: a small helper class for grey, less important text. HOW: put class muted on any element and it uses the - -muted */
/* colour. .small below does the same for a smaller font (.8rem = 80% of normal). IMPROVE: none needed. */
.muted { color: var(--muted); }
.small { font-size: .8rem; }
/* WHY: kindness for people who get sick from motion; they ask their system to reduce animation. HOW: the media query */
/* matches that setting and makes every animation and transition last 0.01ms (almost nothing). !important makes it win */
/* over other rules. IMPROVE: test every new animation with this on. */
@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) {
  * { animation-duration: .01ms !important; transition-duration: .01ms !important; }
}

/* ---------- 3. BUTTONS & INPUTS ----------
   WHY: 40px+ touch targets so thumbs can hit them; one shared style keeps the UI consistent.
        :focus-visible draws a clear outline for people who use the keyboard (Tab key).
   IMPROVE: swap the text symbols for inline SVG icons for a sharper look. */
/* WHY: buttons, inputs and selects normally ignore the page font and colour. HOW: font: inherit and color: inherit copy */
/* the surrounding text style, so the form controls match the theme (also in dark mode). IMPROVE: none needed. */
button, input, select {
  font: inherit; color: inherit;
}
/* WHY: one shared button look so every button is easy to tap (40px is a comfortable finger size). HOW: */
/* min-width/min-height set the smallest size, padding adds side space, the border uses the theme - -line colour, */
/* border-radius rounds corners, cursor shows the hand. IMPROVE: use CSS variables for the radius. */
button {
  min-width: 40px; min-height: 40px;
  padding: 0 12px;
  background: var(--bg);
  border: 1px solid var(--line);
  border-radius: 10px;
  cursor: pointer;
}
/* WHY: feedback so the user sees which button they touch. HOW: hover darkens the border to the text colour; :active */
/* (while pressed) shrinks the button to 96%; :disabled makes it faint and removes the hand cursor. IMPROVE: add a short */
/* transition so the change is smooth. */
button:hover { border-color: var(--fg); }
button:active { transform: scale(.96); }
button:disabled { opacity: .35; cursor: default; }
/* WHY: the main action button (like Go) should stand out. HOW: class primary gives it the orange accent background and */
/* border with white bold text. IMPROVE: use a darker orange on hover. */
button.primary { background: var(--accent); border-color: var(--accent); color: #fff; font-weight: 600; }
/* WHY: keyboard users need to see where they are. HOW: :focus-visible only shows when the Tab key was used; it draws a */
/* 2px orange outline 2px away from the control. IMPROVE: check the outline has enough contrast in dark mode. */
button:focus-visible, input:focus-visible, select:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--accent); outline-offset: 2px; }
/* WHY: text boxes should look like the buttons and fill the row. HOW: width 100% stretches them, a theme background and */
/* border match the site; font-size 16px prevents the iPhone from zooming when you tap the box. IMPROVE: add a */
/* placeholder colour rule. */
input[type="text"] {
  width: 100%; min-height: 40px; padding: 0 12px;
  background: var(--bg); border: 1px solid var(--line); border-radius: 10px;
  font-size: 16px;                              /* WHY: 16px stops iOS Safari zooming on focus */
}
/* WHY: show clearly which text box is active. HOW: on focus, draw an orange outline and hide the normal border */
/* (transparent) so there are not two lines. IMPROVE: none needed. */
input[type="text"]:focus { outline: 2px solid var(--accent); border-color: transparent; }

/* ---------- 4. BROWSER VIEW ----------
   WHY: Flex column = fixed address bar on top, page area fills the remaining height.
        100dvh follows the real visible height on phones (100vh is the fallback for old browsers).
   IMPROVE: make the navbar auto-hide on scroll like a real mobile browser. */
/* WHY: the browser screen is a column: the address bar on top, the page below. HOW: display:flex with */
/* flex-direction:column stacks the children; height 100vh is the fallback, then 100dvh (the real visible height on */
/* phones) overrides it when supported. IMPROVE: none needed. */
#browser { display: flex; flex-direction: column; height: 100vh; height: 100dvh; }
/* WHY: the top address bar with buttons. HOW: a flex row that centres items vertically with 6px gaps. padding-top adds */
/* the phone notch space (- -safe-t) on top of 8px. A thin line under it separates it from the page. IMPROVE: make it */
/* auto-hide when scrolling. */
.navbar {
  display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 6px;
  padding: 8px 8px 8px; padding-top: calc(8px + var(--safe-t));
  border-bottom: 1px solid var(--line);
  background: var(--bg);
  /* ROUND 41 — lets the header hide itself while scrolling through MangaFlow's OWN start/search page (NOT
     while browsing another site inside the iframe — see the long comment in app.js next to "navScrollInit" for
     why that part genuinely cannot be done). WHY max-height instead of transform: this header sits in NORMAL
     page flow (it is not position:fixed), so sliding it away with a transform (the trick #readerBar uses, which
     IS fixed) would leave an empty gap behind where it used to be — #viewport below it would not grow to fill
     that space, since a transform never changes layout. Smoothly shrinking max-height to 0 instead collapses the
     header's own box completely, so the flex:1 #viewport area naturally grows to take the freed room, with no
     gap and no jump. 140px comfortably covers the header's normal one-row desktop height; see the mobile
     override below for the taller two-row phone layout. */
  max-height: 140px; overflow: hidden;
  transition: max-height .22s ease, padding-top .22s ease, padding-bottom .22s ease, border-color .22s ease;
}
.navbar.mf-hide { max-height: 0; padding-top: 0; padding-bottom: 0; border-bottom-color: transparent; }
/* WHY: the address form must take all spare room beside the buttons. HOW: flex:1 means grow to fill; min-width:0 lets */
/* the input shrink on small screens instead of pushing the buttons out. IMPROVE: none needed. */
#addrForm { flex: 1; display: flex; gap: 6px; min-width: 0; }
/* WHY: a thin strip that shows loading progress. HOW: only 3px tall and clear until the class 'on' is added; */
/* overflow:hidden cuts the moving bar when it slides outside. IMPROVE: show real percent when known. */
#loadbar { height: 3px; background: transparent; overflow: hidden; }
/* WHY: the moving orange bar shown while a page loads. HOW: ::before creates an invisible-content box that is 40% wide */
/* and as tall as the strip, filled with the accent colour; the 'slide' animation repeats forever, 1 second long. */
/* IMPROVE: use a gradient for a nicer look. */
#loadbar.on::before {
  content: ""; display: block; height: 100%; width: 40%;
  background: var(--accent); animation: slide 1s linear infinite;
}
/* WHY: defines the 'slide' animation used above. HOW: from/to describe the start and end: the bar starts left of the */
/* strip (-100% of its own width) and ends at 260%, which is past the right edge. IMPROVE: none needed. */
@keyframes slide { from { transform: translateX(-100%); } to { transform: translateX(260%); } }

/* WHY: the area that holds either the start page or the iframe (the website being read). HOW: position:relative lets */
/* children be placed inside it; flex:1 fills the leftover height; overflow:auto adds scrollbars only when needed. */
/* IMPROVE: none needed. */
#viewport { position: relative; flex: 1; overflow: auto; }
/* WHY: the iframe shows the outside manga website. HOW: fill the whole viewport, no border, white background (most sites */
/* assume white), display:block removes the small gap under inline elements. IMPROVE: add a sandbox attribute in HTML for */
/* safety. */
#frame { width: 100%; height: 100%; border: 0; background: #fff; display: block; }
/* WHY: the start page (before a site is opened) should be a neat centred column. HOW: max-width 720px, margin 0 auto */
/* centres it, padding gives side space and 100px at the bottom so the floating button does not cover content. Later */
/* overridden to 860px. IMPROVE: merge the two #start rules. */
#start { max-width: 720px; margin: 0 auto; padding: 24px 16px 100px; }

/* History / bookmark rows: bold title on top, small grey line under it (site, chapter, time). */
/* WHY: the lists of history and bookmarks. HOW: a flex column with 6px gaps between rows. IMPROVE: add a search box for */
/* long lists. */
.list { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 6px; }
/* WHY: each history or bookmark row is a button. HOW: .list .item is a column with the title above the small line; */
/* align-items flex-start keeps text on the left; width 100% and min-height 52px make a big tap target. IMPROVE: add a */
/* delete swipe. */
.list .item {
  display: flex; flex-direction: column; align-items: flex-start; gap: 2px;
  width: 100%; min-height: 52px; padding: 8px 12px; text-align: left;
}
/* WHY: long titles must not break the layout. HOW: .t is the bold title; overflow hidden + text-overflow ellipsis + */
/* white-space nowrap cut the text on one line and add ... at the end. .s on the next line is the same for the small grey */
/* subtitle. IMPROVE: show the full title in a tooltip. */
.item .t { font-weight: 600; max-width: 100%; overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis; white-space: nowrap; }
.item .s { font-size: .78rem; color: var(--muted); max-width: 100%; overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis; white-space: nowrap; }

/* Floating "Reading mode" button (bottom-right corner).
   WHY: always reachable with the thumb; z-index keeps it above the iframe.
   IMPROVE: show how many chapters were detected, e.g. "Reading mode (120)". */
/* WHY: the floating Reading mode button. HOW: position:fixed pins it to the screen corner (right 16px, bottom 18px plus */
/* phone safe space); z-index:20 keeps it above the iframe; 999px radius makes a pill shape; accent colours and a shadow */
/* make it pop. IMPROVE: show how many chapters were found. */
#fabRead {
  position: fixed; right: 16px; bottom: calc(18px + var(--safe-b)); z-index: 20;
  height: 48px; padding: 0 18px; border-radius: 999px;
  background: var(--accent); border-color: var(--accent); color: #fff; font-weight: 700;
  box-shadow: 0 8px 24px rgba(0, 0, 0, .35);
}

/* ROUND 39/40 — "Open on <site>" pinned button. WHY: a quick, always-reachable way to jump from a manga site shown
   inside MangaFlow's mini-browser to that exact page on the REAL site, in a new tab (useful when a button or
   script on the original page cannot work through the proxy). HOW: position:fixed, pinned just below the navbar
   on the right; hidden by default (index.html), only un-hidden by app.js (updateNav) while an actual external
   page — not the start page, not a search list — is on screen, so it never gets in the way otherwise.
   ROUND 40 FIX — this used to be a wide pill with the text "Open original site" on it, and on phones a media
   query moved it down near the BOTTOM of the screen (to dodge the navbar wrapping onto 2 rows there), which put
   it floating in the middle of the actual page content, right next to the "Reading mode" button — the two
   overlapped and looked messy (see the screenshot that reported this). HOW (fix): the button is now the exact
   same small SQUARE icon-button shape as its neighbours in the header (Back/Forward/Reload/Star/Theme/Settings —
   see the plain `button{...}` rule near the top of this file, which it now matches instead of overriding with
   its own pill look), just the single &#8599; arrow with no label text, so it is small enough to stay pinned at
   the TOP RIGHT, under the header, on every screen size — it never needs to move to the bottom any more.
   The only thing that changes between desktop and phone is the "top" offset, because the header itself grows
   taller on a phone (the address bar wraps onto its own row above the row of small buttons there — see the
   "@media (max-width:760px) { .navbar {...} }" rule above); the offset below is just tall enough to clear
   whichever layout the header is currently using. z-index sits above the iframe like #fabRead.
   IMPROVE: read the header's real height with getBoundingClientRect() instead of these two fixed numbers, so it
   never needs adjusting again if the header's own height changes. */
#btnOrigSite {
  position: fixed; top: calc(58px + var(--safe-t)); right: 8px; z-index: 19;
  width: 40px; height: 40px; min-width: 40px; min-height: 40px; padding: 0;
  display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center;
  font-size: 1.05rem; line-height: 1;
  box-shadow: 0 3px 10px rgba(0, 0, 0, .3);
}
#btnOrigSite:hover, #btnOrigSite:focus-visible { border-color: var(--accent); color: var(--accent); }
/* WHY: on a narrow screen the navbar wraps into 2 rows (address pill on its own row, then the small buttons row
   below it), so the header is taller there — this pushes the button down far enough to clear BOTH rows instead
   of sitting on top of them. right stays the same 8px so it lines up with the header's own right edge. */
@media (max-width: 760px) { #btnOrigSite { top: calc(106px + var(--safe-t)); right: 8px; } }

/* ---------- 4b. SEARCH PILL + FLOATING SEARCH BAR (small screens) ----------
   WHY: on a phone the long address input was squeezed next to six buttons and showed almost nothing.
        Under 760px wide the input is hidden, the navbar wraps into two rows, and a full-width "pill"
        shows the current address. Tapping the pill opens a floating bar with a big input + Go button.
   HOW: #addrPill is hidden on wide screens and #addrForm is hidden on narrow screens (media query below).
   IMPROVE: let the pill show the page title instead of the address. */
/* WHY: the phone-sized fake address box (the pill). HOW: hidden by default (display:none); when shown it is a flex row */
/* with an icon and text, round (999px). min-width:0 allows the text to shrink. IMPROVE: show the page title in it. */
#addrPill {
  display: none; align-items: center; gap: 8px;
  min-width: 0; padding: 0 12px; text-align: left;
  border-radius: 999px;
}
/* WHY: keep the first span (the icon) from shrinking. HOW: flex:none means do not grow and do not shrink. IMPROVE: none */
/* needed. */
#addrPill span:first-child { flex: none; }
/* WHY: the pill text shows the current address, which can be long. HOW: flex:1 fills the pill; min-width:0 + overflow */
/* hidden + ellipsis + nowrap cut long text with ...; muted grey colour. IMPROVE: show only the site name. */
#pillText { flex: 1; min-width: 0; overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis; white-space: nowrap; color: var(--muted); }
/* WHY: on screens 760px or narrower there is no room for the long address input. HOW: the media query switches layout: */
/* the navbar wraps to two rows, the form hides, the pill shows first (order:-1) at full width (flex: 1 0 100%), and the */
/* other buttons share row two evenly. IMPROVE: use a variable for 760px. */
@media (max-width: 760px) {
  .navbar { flex-wrap: wrap; row-gap: 6px; max-height: 220px; }   /* ROUND 41: taller cap for the 2-row mobile layout */
  #addrForm { display: none; }
  #addrPill { display: flex; order: -1; flex: 1 0 100%; min-height: 44px; }
  .navbar > button:not(#addrPill) { flex: 1 1 0; }      /* the six small buttons share the second row evenly */
}
/* WHY: a dark layer behind the floating search bar so it stands out. HOW: position:fixed with inset:0 covers the whole */
/* screen; z-index 79 is just under the search box (80); the black is 45% see-through. IMPROVE: close the search when the */
/* shade is tapped (check app.js). */
#popShade { position: fixed; inset: 0; z-index: 79; background: rgba(0, 0, 0, .45); }
/* WHY: the floating search bar opened from the pill. HOW: fixed at the top centre (left 50% + translateX(-50%) centres */
/* it); width is the smaller of 680px or screen minus 20px; padding, theme colours, rounded corners and shadow make it */
/* look like a card. IMPROVE: slide it in with an animation. */
#searchPop {
  position: fixed; z-index: 80; left: 50%; transform: translateX(-50%);
  top: calc(10px + var(--safe-t)); width: min(680px, calc(100vw - 20px));
  padding: 10px; background: var(--bg); border: 1px solid var(--line); border-radius: 14px; box-shadow: var(--shadow);
}
/* WHY: layout inside the floating search bar. HOW: a flex row with gaps; the input grows (flex:1), may shrink */
/* (min-width:0) and is 46px tall; the button matches that height. IMPROVE: none needed. */
#popForm { display: flex; gap: 6px; align-items: center; }
#popForm input { flex: 1; min-width: 0; min-height: 46px; }
#popForm button { min-height: 46px; }

/* ---------- 5. READER BAR (title space at the top) ----------
   WHY: fixed at the top so the manga name is always visible. Blur makes text readable over pages.
   IMPROVE: add a tiny cover thumbnail next to the title. */
/* WHY: the title bar shown at the top while reading. HOW: position:fixed with top/left/right 0 pins it across the top; */
/* z-index 30 puts it over the pictures; - -bar gives a see-through background and backdrop-filter blurs what is behind */
/* (the -webkit- line is for Safari). IMPROVE: add a cover thumbnail. */
#readerBar {
  position: fixed; top: 0; left: 0; right: 0; z-index: 30;
  background: var(--bar);
  -webkit-backdrop-filter: blur(8px); backdrop-filter: blur(8px);
  border-bottom: 1px solid var(--line);
  /* WHY: leave space on top. HOW: padding-top = phone notch space + 3px for the progress line. The transition makes the */
  /* bar slide smoothly in .28s; will-change tells the browser to prepare for moving it so it is smooth. IMPROVE: remove */
  /* will-change if it uses too much memory. */
  padding-top: calc(var(--safe-t) + 3px);                 /* 3px = room for the progress line at the very top */
  transition: transform .28s ease;                        /* ROUND 9: the bar SLIDES up (see section 6) */
  will-change: transform;
}
/* WHY: the main row of the reader bar (exit, title, buttons). HOW: a flex row, centred vertically, 8px gaps and padding. */
/* IMPROVE: none needed. */
.rb-row { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 8px; padding: 6px 10px; }
/* WHY: the title area should take all the spare room in the row. HOW: flex:1 grows, min-width:0 allows shrinking, */
/* text-align:center centres; the opacity transition lets it fade (dimmed while scrolling). h1 below has no margin, 1rem */
/* text and one line with ... for long names. IMPROVE: let long titles scroll sideways. */
.rb-title { flex: 1; min-width: 0; text-align: center; transition: opacity .25s; }
.rb-title h1 { margin: 0; font-size: 1rem; white-space: nowrap; overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis; }
/* WHY: #rSub is the small sub-title line (for example the chapter info). HOW: smaller font (.75rem) in grey. Redefined */
/* later in round 11 with a pill look. IMPROVE: merge both rules. */
#rSub { font-size: .75rem; color: var(--muted); }
/* ROUND 8: search / link row inside the reader bar. */
/* WHY: the search / link row inside the reader bar. HOW: a flex row with side padding; the input grows and is 40px tall, */
/* the button also 40px tall. IMPROVE: hide the row until the user taps a search icon. */
.rb-search { display: flex; gap: 6px; padding: 0 10px 8px; }
.rb-search input { flex: 1; min-width: 0; min-height: 40px; }
.rb-search button { min-height: 40px; }
/* ROUND 9: the reading-progress line is pinned to the very top edge of the screen (position: fixed), outside the bar.
   WHY: the bar slides up when you scroll down; the line used to stay behind in the middle of the page. Now it is always at
        the top edge, thin (3 px) and on top of everything, so it never covers the art.
   HOW: app.js updateCurrent() sets the width of the <i> inside. top = safe-area so a phone notch does not hide it. */
/* WHY: a thin reading-progress line at the top of the screen. HOW: fixed to the top edge (below any phone notch), full */
/* width, 3px tall, above everything (z-index 35); pointer-events:none lets taps pass through it. Made 4px later. */
/* IMPROVE: show percent text on hover. */
/* ROUND 31 - THE LINE IS ALWAYS AT THE VERY TOP EDGE OF THE SCREEN, whatever the mode or the device.
   WHY: the owner (2026-10-31): "in full screen on my phone the line does not go to the top, it shows in between the chapters; it must always be at the top, on every device and browser, also
        while scrolling down". Until round 30 the line used top: var(--safe-t) (the phone-notch space). In the normal page that space is 0 or is covered by the title bar, so it looked right.
        But in full screen the phone browser reports a real notch / status-bar space (e.g. 30 px), the title bar is hidden (round 29c), and the line floated 30 px down INSIDE the pictures.
        The same happened in normal mode while the title bar slid away on scrolling down.
   HOW: top is now plain 0 for every case: normal, full screen (body.fs), scrolling, F11, installed-app windows. The title bar below keeps its own notch space (padding-top), so nothing else moves.
        A few pixels of the line can sit under a camera hole: that is fine (the line is thin and spans the whole width).
   TEST: R31-1 .. R31-3 in test/ui.test.js put a 32 px notch space on a phone and a computer and measure the line in normal, full screen and scrolled states.
   IMPROVE: if a phone ever hides the line under its status bar, add a second thin line at the bottom edge as a fallback. */
#progress { position: fixed; top: 0; left: 0; right: 0; height: 3px; z-index: 35; background: transparent; pointer-events: none; }
/* WHY: the coloured part of the progress line. HOW: the <i> element starts at width 0 and app.js changes the width; the */
/* .12s linear transition makes growth smooth. IMPROVE: none needed. */
#progress i { display: block; height: 100%; width: 0; background: var(--accent); transition: width .12s linear; }

/* ---------- 6. AUTO-HIDE WHILE SCROLLING DOWN ----------
   WHY: app.js adds the class "scrolling" to <body> when you scroll DOWN. Buttons (exit, chapter list,
        theme, arrow keys) fade out so nothing blocks the art. They come back ONLY when you scroll UP
        (mouse wheel up, finger drag down, Up arrow key) or reach the top. The manga title stays (dimmed).
   IMPROVE: make the 14 px "dead zone" in app.js a setting. */
/* WHY: any element with class ui-hide can fade out while scrolling. HOW: the transition animates opacity over .25s; the */
/* next rule sets opacity 0 and turns off clicking when body has the class 'scrolling'. IMPROVE: add a short delay so it */
/* does not flicker on tiny scrolls. */
.ui-hide { transition: opacity .25s; }
body.scrolling .ui-hide { opacity: 0; pointer-events: none; }
/* ROUND 9: while you scroll down the WHOLE bar (title, buttons, search row) slides up out of the screen. The progress line
   is a separate element pinned to the top edge, so it simply stays there as a thin line. The bar stops catching clicks
   while it is away, so taps in the top area still scroll the chapter. It slides back when you scroll up. */
/* WHY: while scrolling down, the whole title bar leaves the screen so it does not cover the art. HOW: when body has */
/* 'scrolling', the bar moves up 110% of its height (translateY) and ignores taps; the progress line stays slightly */
/* see-through (.9). IMPROVE: add a small handle to bring the bar back. */
body.scrolling #readerBar { transform: translateY(-110%); pointer-events: none; }
body.scrolling #progress { opacity: .9; }

/* ---------- 7. CHAPTER COLUMN (centered, "floating") ----------
   WHY: margin auto centres each chapter; border + soft shadow make it look like a floating sheet.
        On phones it goes full width and loses the rounded corners to give the art maximum size.
   IMPROVE: add a "fit height" mode that scales each page to the screen height. */
/* WHY: #stream is the box that holds all chapters. HOW: padding 0 so chapters touch the screen sides when needed. */
/* IMPROVE: none needed. */
#stream { padding: 0; }
/* ROUND 9: the earlier-chapters bar sits above the stream and also provides the empty space under the fixed title bar. */
/* WHY: the area above the first chapter: it holds the load-earlier-chapters button and also leaves room under the fixed */
/* title bar. HOW: big min-height and top padding add space for the bar (112px + notch); the flex column centres the */
/* content with 6px gaps. IMPROVE: compute the bar height with JavaScript. */
#prevBar {
  min-height: calc(112px + var(--safe-t) + 64px); padding: calc(112px + var(--safe-t) + 10px) 12px 10px;   /* space for the bar + the controls */
  display: flex; flex-direction: column; align-items: center; gap: 6px; text-align: center;
}
/* WHY: make the load-earlier button easy to tap. HOW: 44px tall with side padding. The next rule hides it entirely when */
/* disabled (nothing to load) so only the text remains. IMPROVE: none needed. */
#prevBar button { min-height: 44px; padding: 0 18px; }
#prevBar button:disabled { display: none; }               /* nothing earlier to load: only the text is shown */
/* WHY: each chapter looks like a floating sheet. HOW: width is the smaller of the chosen width (- -w) or 100%; margin 0 */
/* auto centres it and adds 56px below; theme background, thin border, rounded corners and shadow; overflow:hidden clips */
/* pictures to the rounded corners. IMPROVE: add a fit-height mode. */
.chapter {
  width: min(var(--w), 100%); margin: 0 auto 56px;
  background: var(--bg);
  border: 1px solid var(--line); border-radius: 12px;
  box-shadow: var(--shadow);
  overflow: hidden;
}
/* WHY: on phones the chapter should use the full width. HOW: at 700px or narrower, remove rounded corners and side */
/* borders and use less space below. IMPROVE: none needed. */
@media (max-width: 700px) {
  .chapter { border-radius: 0; border-left: 0; border-right: 0; margin-bottom: 36px; }
}

/* Chapter header: manga name, chapter number, chapter title - at the start of every chapter. */
/* WHY: the top part of a chapter that shows its name. HOW: centred text, padding for air, a thin line below to separate */
/* it from the pictures. IMPROVE: add the cover picture. */
.ch-head { text-align: center; padding: 30px 16px 22px; border-bottom: 1px solid var(--line); }
/* WHY: the manga name should look like a small label. HOW: small font, letter-spacing for wide letters, */
/* text-transform:uppercase makes capitals, grey colour. .ch-num below is the big chapter number: clamp(1.5rem, 5vw, */
/* 2.1rem) grows with the screen but stays between two limits. IMPROVE: none needed. */
.ch-manga { font-size: .8rem; letter-spacing: .12em; text-transform: uppercase; color: var(--muted); }
.ch-num { font-size: clamp(1.5rem, 5vw, 2.1rem); font-weight: 800; margin: 4px 0; }
/* WHY: the chapter title is less important than the number. HOW: grey colour only. IMPROVE: none needed. */
.ch-title { color: var(--muted); }

/* Pages. WHY: display:block removes the tiny gap browsers leave under images.
   The grey min-height box reserves space so the page does not jump while images load. */
/* WHY: the manga pictures. HOW: display:block removes the small gap browsers leave under images; width 100% fits the */
/* column; height:auto keeps the picture shape. IMPROVE: add loading='lazy' in JS for speed. */
img.page { display: block; width: 100%; height: auto; }
/* WHY: before an image loads, the page would be tiny and then jump. HOW: :not(.loaded) matches images without the class */
/* 'loaded'; they get a 260px tall light-grey box (rgba 128 grey, 12% strong). IMPROVE: use the real image ratio if */
/* known. */
img.page:not(.loaded) { min-height: 260px; background: rgba(128, 128, 128, .12); }
/* WHY: the footer of each chapter. HOW: centred grey text with padding and a line above. .ch-msg below is a message box */
/* (centred, grey, big padding); its .row holds buttons in a centred row. IMPROVE: none needed. */
.ch-end { text-align: center; color: var(--muted); padding: 26px 12px; border-top: 1px solid var(--line); }
.ch-msg { text-align: center; padding: 40px 16px; color: var(--muted); }
.ch-msg .row { display: flex; gap: 8px; justify-content: center; margin-top: 12px; }

/* WHY: a loading circle. HOW: a 28px box with a grey ring (border) where only the top is orange; border-radius 50% makes */
/* it round; the 'spin' animation rotates it forever. IMPROVE: none needed. */
.spinner {
  width: 28px; height: 28px; margin: 0 auto 10px;
  border: 3px solid var(--line); border-top-color: var(--accent); border-radius: 50%;
  animation: spin .8s linear infinite;
}
/* WHY: defines the spin animation. HOW: it only needs the end state: rotate 360 degrees; the start is the normal */
/* position. IMPROVE: none needed. */
@keyframes spin { to { transform: rotate(360deg); } }

/* WHY: #sentinel is an invisible marker near the end; JavaScript watches it to load the next chapter. HOW: just 2px tall */
/* so it exists in the layout. IMPROVE: none needed. */
#sentinel { height: 2px; }
/* Download bar at the end of the page (round 2). */
/* WHY: the download area at the end of the chapters. HOW: same width as chapters and centred; padding, centred text and */
/* a line above. Its paragraphs get 6px margin; its buttons are bigger (50px tall, 1rem text). IMPROVE: show the file */
/* size estimate here. */
#dlBar { width: min(var(--w), 100%); margin: 0 auto; padding: 22px 16px; text-align: center; border-top: 1px solid var(--line); }
#dlBar p { margin: 6px 0; }
#dlBar button { min-height: 50px; padding: 0 24px; font-size: 1rem; }
/* WHY: the very last message. HOW: centred grey text; bottom padding of 150px (+ safe area) leaves room so the floating */
/* keys do not cover it. IMPROVE: none needed. */
#theEnd { text-align: center; padding: 20px 16px calc(150px + var(--safe-b)); color: var(--muted); }

/* ---------- 8. FLOATING READER KEYS (round 9: ONE horizontal row of round 3D buttons, bottom-RIGHT corner) ----------
   WHY: the person asked for the keys in a single HORIZONTAL row (reload this chapter, reload all, previous, next, end), in the
        right corner, and as 3D CIRCLES instead of squares.
   HOW: flex row. Each key is a circle (border-radius 50%). The 3D look comes from three things:
          1. a radial-gradient (light spot top-left) that makes it look like a ball / dome,
          2. a solid shadow under it (box-shadow 0 5px 0 = the "thickness" of the button),
          3. inset highlights. Pressing moves the key down 4px and shrinks the thickness, like a real key.
        Side is switchable in Settings (body[data-side]); default is RIGHT (round 9).
   WHERE: buttons live in index.html (<nav id="side">); app.js section 14 wires the clicks and the End key.
   IMPROVE: add a click sound, or small legends under the keys.
   ROUND 28 NOTE (so this old text does not mislead you): this block describes ROUND 9. Later blocks further down this file win over it:
        the two reload keys are gone (the reload wheel, reload-wheel.js, replaced them and sits TOP LEFT, see "ROUND 19 ADDITIONS" and "ROUND 20" near the end),
        the right-hand column under the title bar is now: download pill (#dock), full-screen icon (#fsRead); at the bottom edge the chapter slider
        (chapter-slider.js) stands at the bottom RIGHT and the Top / End slider (edge-slider.js) at the bottom LEFT (they swap sides with the "buttons side" setting).
        The keys that are still in <nav id="side"> are Top, previous, next and End (#btnTop, #btnPrev, #btnNext, #btnEnd); the sliders hide the ones they replace. */
/* ROUND 9b: #side is a click-through strip across the bottom. The reload keys (.kg-l) sit in the LEFT corner and the previous /
   next / end keys (.kg-r) form one horizontal row in the RIGHT corner. WHY a strip: both groups hide and show together
   (one .ui-hide), and pointer-events:none lets you tap the pictures between the groups. */
/* WHY: the strip that holds the floating reader keys. HOW: fixed across the bottom with 12px side margins; - -key sets */
/* the key size (50px); flex row with space-between puts one group left and one right; pointer-events:none lets taps pass */
/* between the groups. IMPROVE: let users drag the keys. */
#side {
  position: fixed; bottom: calc(14px + var(--safe-b)); left: 12px; right: 12px; z-index: 30;
  --key: 40px;                                       /* round 13: leaner keys (was 50 px) */
  display: flex; flex-direction: row; justify-content: space-between; align-items: flex-end;
  pointer-events: none;
}
/* WHY: each key group (.kg). HOW: a flex row, no wrapping, 9px gaps; pointer-events:auto turns clicking back on for the */
/* keys themselves. IMPROVE: none needed. */
~~~~~~
